deep.reconstruction:
Definitions. The page defines the Rogers–Ramanujan continued fraction. Writing x = q:

f(x) = x^{1/5} * prod_{n>=1} (1-x^{5n-1})(1-x^{5n-4}) / [(1-x^{5n-2})(1-x^{5n-3})]
     = x^{1/5}/(1+ x/(1+ x^2/(1+ x^3/(1+ ...)))).

The numerator factors are (1-x)(1-x^4)(1-x^6)(1-x^9)(1-x^11)...; the denominator factors are (1-x^2)(1-x^3)(1-x^7)(1-x^8)(1-x^12).... So f = R(q), the Rogers–Ramanujan continued fraction. The product form is the Rogers (1894) / Ramanujan product formula. It follows from the Rogers–Ramanujan identities on the previous page (folio 88): G(x) = 1/((1-x)(1-x^6)...(1-x^4)(1-x^9)...) and H(x) similarly, with R = x^{1/5} H/G.

The page then lists, without proof, five modular equations relating P = R(q) to Q = R of a transformed argument.

I. Q = R(-q):
   PQ(P+Q)^4 + P^2Q^2(P+Q)^2 + 2P^3Q^3 = (P+Q)(1 - P^5Q^5).
   Here (-q)^{1/5} = -q^{1/5} (real branch).

II. Q = R(q^2):
   P^2 - Q + PQ^2(P^2+Q) = 0.
   Equivalently (Q - P^2)/(Q + P^2) = PQ^2.

III. Q = R(q^3):
   (P^3 - Q)(1 + PQ^3) + 3P^2Q^2 = 0.
   Equivalently (Q - P^3)(1 + PQ^3) = 3P^2Q^2.

IV. Q = R(q^4):
   (P^5+Q^5)(PQ-1) + PQ + P^5Q^5 = 5P^2Q^2(PQ-1)^2.

V. Q = R(q^5):
   P^5 = Q(1 - 2Q + 4Q^2 - 3Q^3 + Q^4)/(1 + 3Q + 4Q^2 + 2Q^3 + Q^4).
   This is the icosahedral quintic relation.

Purpose. The page is a catalogue of modular equations of degrees 2, 3, 4 and 5 (and the q -> -q transformation) for R(q). It continues the previous page, which held the Rogers–Ramanujan identities and the R^5 / eta-quotient formula.

My checks: I verified the leading terms by hand with t = q^{1/5}, using R(q) = t(1 - q + q^2 - q^4 + q^5 - ...).
- II: P^2 - Q ~ -2t^7 cancels PQ^2(P^2+Q) ~ +2t^7.
- III: P^3 - Q ~ -3t^8 cancels 3P^2Q^2 ~ +3t^8.
- IV: LHS ~ -q + 5q^2 + q - q^2 + q^2 = 5q^2, and RHS ~ 5q^2.
- I: both sides equal -2t^6 - 2t^16 + O(t^26).
All five agree with the forms published in the literature.
errors: No mathematical errors detected; leading-order series checks of I–IV agree, and V is the standard icosahedral relation.
Relation I needs the branch convention (-x)^{1/5} = -x^{1/5}; Ramanujan leaves this implicit.
No proofs are given; the results are stated only.

results.what: Product representation of the Rogers–Ramanujan continued fraction R(q) = q^{1/5} prod (1-q^{5n-1})(1-q^{5n-4})/((1-q^{5n-2})(1-q^{5n-3}))
results.usually_credited_to: Rogers (1894), Ramanujan (independently, first letter to Hardy 1913)

results.what: Relation between R(q) and R(-q): uv(u+v)^4 + u^2v^2(u+v)^2 + 2u^3v^3 = (u+v)(1-u^5v^5)
results.modern_name: Modular relation between R(q) and R(-q)
results.usually_credited_to: Ramanujan (unpublished manuscripts / lost notebook); proofs by Andrews–Berndt and others

results.what: Degree-2 modular equation (v-u^2)/(v+u^2) = uv^2 for u=R(q), v=R(q^2)
results.modern_name: Modular equation of degree 2 for the Rogers–Ramanujan continued fraction
Modular equation of degree 3 for R(q)
results.usually_credited_to: Ramanujan; proofs by Rogers / Andrews–Berndt–Jacobsen–Lamphere and later authors

results.what: Degree-4 modular equation (u^5+v^5)(uv-1) + uv + u^5v^5 = 5u^2v^2(uv-1)^2 for v=R(q^4)
results.modern_name: Modular equation of degree 4 for R(q)
results.usually_credited_to: Ramanujan (lost notebook material); proved by e.g. Kang / Andrews–Berndt
Ramanujan (second letter to Hardy, 1913); proof Rogers (1920), Watson (1929)

deep.surprise_reason: All six statements are well-known Ramanujan results. They appear in his letters, notebooks and lost-notebook material, which includes the Trinity manuscripts published by Narosa in 1988. They are proved in Andrews–Berndt, Lost Notebook Part I, Ch. 1, and Berndt's Notebooks Part III. This page is one of the original sources, not a new attribution.

checkable.asserts: Relation II: the series vanishes identically, with P=R(q), Q=R(q^2), q=t^5.
Relation I vanishes for Q=R(-q), with branch (-q)^{1/5} = -q^{1/5}.
The product equals the continued fraction (to the truncation order).
